npc:anastasia-hartwell.text: Anastasia Hartwell. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell trains Forsaken and Horde mages in the arcane arts. She guides spellcasters in their studies and directs magical research and field work across Lordaeron and beyond. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell teaches Forsaken and Horde mages to channel arcane energies. Though Lordaeron has fallen to ruin, former human practitioners such as Anastasia preserve their scholarly traditions in undeath. She demands discipline in the practice of magic. Careless incantations can consume the untrained. Anastasia sends promising students into the field as well as teaching them spells. At Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades, mages gather snapdragons to learn how far the plague has spread. In the Apothecarium, they visit Algernon's alchemist shop to capture invisible creatures of pure magic behind a strange disturbance. Her assignments bring them face to face with magic's dangers, even within their own city. Anastasia's connections reach beyond Tirisfal. As Horde spellcasters grow more skilled, she coordinates with trainers in distant lands, including Deino in Orgrimmar. She also directs advanced students to solitary masters such as Tabetha in the swamplands of Dustwallow Marsh. Her guidance keeps Forsaken mages connected to the Horde's wider magical pursuits.

npc:apothecary-johaan.text: Apothecary Johaan. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan works on a plague for the Forsaken. The Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas have set him to lethal experiments on local plants and animals. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan works openly for the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, he follows direct orders to create biological and alchemical weapons. The Forsaken hope these weapons will secure their fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

npc:apothecary-renferrel.text: Apothecary Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel studies Silverpine’s corrupted wildlife and undead threats. He advances Forsaken alchemy, and travelers bring him volatile reagents and help investigate Scourge remnants. At the Sepulcher, Renferrel leads field research for the Royal Apothecary Society in Silverpine Forest. The society’s grand laboratories and high leadership are in Undercity, while he works in the field. He gathers native biological specimens, refines potent concoctions, and studies the grim ecology along Lordaeron’s western border.

npc:aramis-hammerhand.text: Aramis Hammerhand. In Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand teaches the newly risen Forsaken to fight with the Holy Light. They can call on its power, but it burns their decayed flesh and demands fierce discipline. In Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand guides Forsaken who still hold to their former faith. Before the Scourge swept across the north, many people of Lordaeron answered the Silver Hand's call. Aramis survived Lordaeron's fall, then rose into undeath. He kept the martial and spiritual teachings of his former life, and now guides others who will not surrender their devotion. For the Forsaken, channeling the Holy Light takes fierce will. Its power burns necrotic flesh and stirs long-dead nerves into excruciating pain. Aramis teaches new paladins that faith means enduring this torment. He asks them to face the physical and spiritual cost of wielding a force opposed to their undead nature.

npc:arugal.text: Arugal. In Shadowfang Keep, Arugal commands the worgen he summoned against the Scourge. Madness and grief have made the former Dalaran wizard their self-proclaimed father, while his power threatens Silverpine Forest. Before Lordaeron fell, Arugal belonged to the Kirin Tor. Some peers, including Dalar Dawnweaver, called him a charlatan who leaned on enchanted trinkets to make up for weak spellcraft. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal searched for a weapon that could halt the undead. He used research by the late Dalaran mage Ur to pierce the veil between realms and summon the worgen. The ravenous beasts tore through the Scourge, but no one could contain their ferocity. Soon their hunger turned against innocent mortals. The worgen slaughtered the Scourge, then turned on the wizards who summoned them. They besieged the ancestral seat of Baron Silverlaine, whose keep fell to their claws and fangs. Silverlaine and his retainers died in the massacre. Guilt shattered Arugal's mind, but he did not flee his creation. He adopted the beasts as his own offspring and renamed the fortress Shadowfang Keep. There he holds the ramparts, surrounded by ghostly victims and loyal hound-packs.

npc:baine-bloodhoof.text: Baine Bloodhoof. In Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof guards his people and Mulgore. Cairne leads from Thunder Bluff, while Baine directs the village’s defense against gnolls and outside threats. Baine Bloodhoof grew up traveling with his nomadic people as Cairne’s son. They settled in Mulgore’s grasslands, where centaur clans remained a threat. After the Third War, Khiragg’s warband captured Baine, and grief nearly kept Cairne from leading the new settlements. Rexxar freed Baine, restoring Cairne’s spirit. Then the tauren stood with Thrall’s Horde against the invading Kul Tirans and secured their foothold on the continent. Baine lives among his kin in Bloodhoof Village, not at the capital mesas. As Cairne grows older, Baine carries more responsibility for the people and represents the next generation of tauren leadership. He directs braves and visiting allies against Palemane gnolls troubling the borders. He also watches for outside influences that threaten Mulgore’s natural balance. Baine faces encroachers who give little thought to spiritual balance. In eastern Mulgore, the goblin Venture Company cuts into the sacred landscape. Dwarven prospectors from Bael Modan dig ancestral soil at the Bael'dun Digsite. Baine urges a firm but measured response: warn the miners and destroy their equipment instead of rushing into needless bloodshed. He says their violent digging hurts the spirits of the earth, but the miners refuse to listen.

npc:bethor-iceshard.text: Bethor Iceshard. In the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard directs the Magic Quarter's arcane and shadow practitioners. He holds authority in Sylvanas's realm, though old friendships still mark his past. From the Temple of the Damned in the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard directs arcane and shadow practitioners. His keen mind and icy resolve earn respect and fear. His political and magical authority reaches magistrates across Lordaeron. He sends Forsaken agents after valuable grimoires and arcane disturbances, and against rival powers that threaten the Undercity's rule.

npc:brewmaster-drohn.text: Brewmaster Drohn. Above Ratchet's docks, Brewmaster Drohn tends his brewing craft. The orc lives just uphill from the port, making potent drinks with methods tied to the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. Travelers who find discarded kegs across Kalimdor are sent to Drohn's porch. Brewmaster Drohn brews from his home on the hill above Ratchet's goblin docks. Rather than devote himself to combat, the orc has given his craft to brewing. He lives peacefully in the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While many orcs favor coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn works with rare ingredients, carefully balanced flavors, and methods seldom practiced among his kin. Brewmaster Drohn learned brewing through a mentor who studied under Chen Stormstout, the pandaren wanderer who fought beside Rexxar and the Horde during the founding of Durotar. Chen also taught Drohn to make Trogg Ale. When travelers find Chen's discarded kegs in the wilds, Drohn is the only local authority who can identify their ingredients and recreate the wanderer's potent brews.

npc:brine.text: Brine. On Blackthorn Ridge, Brine guides shaman initiates toward the spirits of water. This orc shaman teaches them to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Brine lives on a hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, far from the Barrens' trading posts. Though dry savannas surround her, she has devoted her life to understanding water. Shaman across the Horde seek her wisdom after mastering earth and fire. She teaches that water calls for patience and perspective, qualities few understand as deeply as she does. In her youth, Brine marched with her orc companions across the Hillsbrad Foothills and fought against human settlements. During the campaign, she came to Tarren Mill and found a humble well fed by fresh spring water. The well stayed in her memory as a sign of life amid devastation. It strengthened a lesson she had learned as a child: even in the darkest sorrow, a small token of hope can still be found.

npc:cairne-bloodhoof.text:
Cairne Bloodhoof. In Thunder Bluff, Cairne Bloodhoof leads the united tauren tribes. The High Chieftain joined their fate to Thrall’s Horde after the orcs helped them escape extinction at centaur hands. Cairne Bloodhoof led the tauren from a life of flight to a home in Mulgore. For generations, centaur marauders hunted the tribes across the Barrens and drove them toward extinction. When Thrall and his orcs reached Kalimdor, Cairne saw a rare nobility in them.

Thrall offered protection and an escort for Cairne’s desperate caravan across the plains. In return, Cairne guided them to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. The tauren settled on Thunder Bluff’s towering mesas, where Cairne united the tribes and gave them a permanent home. Cairne Bloodhoof fought beside Thrall’s Horde and Jaina Proudmoore’s humans against the Burning Legion during the Third War. Grateful to Thrall, Cairne had followed the orcs to Stonetalon Peak. When Admiral Daelin Proudmoore invaded Durotar, Cairne took up arms again beside Rexxar. His captured son, Baine, had been safely recovered. Now one of the Horde’s most respected elders, Cairne remains Thrall’s closest confidant. He offers calm counsel against reckless warmongering.

npc:canaga-earthcaller.text: Canaga Earthcaller. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new Horde shamans toward the spirits of the land and their first totems. Canaga Earthcaller guides Darkspear trolls and orcs who begin the shaman’s path from the red bluffs of the Valley of Trials. He teaches newcomers to quiet their minds and listen to Kalimdor’s rumblings. They prepare earth sapta so they can commune with the spirits. Canaga asks each novice to gather sacred reagents and travel to the local spirit rock in Durotar. There, they drink earth sapta and see the elemental spirits firsthand. Through his guidance, they earn their Earth Totem.

npc:carendin-halgar.text: Carendin Halgar. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar teaches the Forsaken dark arts. His students learn to bind demons from the Twisting Nether, including Voidwalkers and Succubi. Carendin Halgar trains warlocks in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. He demands focus and obedience, and has little patience for failure, hesitation, or weakness. His students pass beyond simple incantations to summon demons and manipulate souls. Under his direction, they learn how the Forsaken make demons serve.

npc:chief-hawkwind.text: Chief Hawkwind. At Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind readies young Shu'halo for life beyond Red Cloud Mesa. He guides their traditional rites in Mulgore and teaches humility, respect for the land, and the strength to protect their people. At Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind prepares young tauren for life beyond Red Cloud Mesa. Fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother on the mesa. Hawkwind oversees their customs and teaches each youth duty and endurance before they leave its safety. Chief Hawkwind begins with humility, not martial glory. He sends initiates to fetch clean spring water and perform simple chores, teaching reverence for nature and their elders. Once they show humility, the braves face tests of martial skill. Their trials test their resolve against aggressive Bristleback quilboar encroaching on the ancestral plains. Danger presses close to Camp Narache. The Bristleback tribe grows bolder along Red Cloud Mesa's perimeter. Hawkwind coordinates the settlement's defense and sends newly proven braves to blunt quilboar assaults and keep the sacred training grounds secure.

npc:coleman-farthing.text: Coleman Farthing. At Brill's Gallows' End Tavern, Coleman Farthing still nurses a hatred born at the Agamand Mills. He served the wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal. He and the other laborers died defending their employers' estate from the Scourge. Now Forsaken, Coleman seeks vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing worked at the Agamand Mills, Tirisfal Glades' largest milling and agricultural operation. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. They urged their household and laborers to take up arms, promising to hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers trusted their masters and stayed. Every last one of them died. Raised into undeath, Coleman Farthing broke free into the Forsaken, but his hatred of the Agamands endured. He blames his former employers' greed and pride for luring their staff into an impossible last stand, as much as he blames the Scourge. From a tavern in Brill, he sends Horde champions to the blighted mills to kill the risen Agamand kin and plunder heirloom weapons from their family crypt. He means to strip away the last of their honor.

npc:dalar-dawnweaver.text:
Dalar Dawnweaver. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver turns his arcane learning against the Forsaken’s enemies. He was an archmage of Dalaran, slain when the Scourge destroyed the city, then freed from the Lich King’s control. Now he studies Dalaran’s lingering presence and seeks to end Archmage Arugal’s madness. Dalar Dawnweaver once held high rank among the Kirin Tor. He walked the Violet Citadel’s halls when Dalaran stood at the height of arcane mastery. The Scourge sacked the city to prepare for Archimonde’s summoning, and Dalar died there.

Raised as a mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge’s grip faltered. Now he keeps an archmage’s keen intellect at the Sepulcher and devotes it to protecting the Forsaken realm. Dalar directs the Sepulcher’s arcane strategy against the many dangers facing Silverpine Forest. To the south, Dalaran wizards occupy Ambermill, pursuing matters he means to uncover and disrupt. Closer by, feral worgen prowl the woods around Shadowfang Keep.

Dalar knows his former colleague, Archmage Arugal, well. He carefully directs efforts to stop Arugal’s beastly creations before they overrun the region.

npc:darsok-swiftdagger.text: Darsok Swiftdagger. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern trails for threats. The orc scout directs Horde fighters against Witchwing harpies in the Dry Hills, whose raids endanger travelers and settlements. He is also an old friend of Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern scrubland from the Crossroads. The roads linking Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens’ northern reaches face raiders and centaur, as well as organized hunters from the sky. Darsok’s anger falls on the Witchwing harpies. Their roosts lie in the Dry Hills, northwest of the Forgotten Pools, where they threaten caravans traveling north. Darsok has an old friend far northwest of the Barrens: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil, a troll who lives at Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, the land the harpies come from. Darsok sends Jin'Zil a letter with news of the harpy campaign. The two friends have not been in touch for many years.

npc:deathguard-dillinger.text: Deathguard Dillinger. At Brill's edge, Deathguard Dillinger watches the town and guides new Forsaken arrivals. He sends recruits to drive Scourge remnants from nearby farms and mills. Deathguard Dillinger guards Brill and guides those arriving from Deathknell. At the town entrance, he points newly awakened undead toward the inn, town hall, and local trainers. Under the Dark Lady's rule, they must learn their way through a changed life. Deathguard Dillinger sends capable recruits to clear mindless Scourge from nearby farms and mills. They cull rotting ghouls and reclaim infested facilities. In doing so, they make Brill's border safer and help the fledgling Forsaken settlements endure the undead threat.

npc:dendrite-starblaze.text: Dendrite Starblaze. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze guides druids who come to Moonglade. As a Cenarion Circle mentor, he welcomes night elf and tauren apprentices. Through him they are summoned to the holy grove to master its rites, from cleansing toxins to communing with nature's forms. When novice druids learn Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to greet them in Nighthaven. He follows the Cenarion Circle's calling beyond the Alliance and Horde. Night elf and tauren druids alike find kinship beneath the haven's boughs, where Kaldorei tradition meets the tauren path. Dendrite guides apprentices into nature's deeper ways. He sends them to examine tainted waters and seek herbs that can cure poison and pestilence. Then he oversees the water trials, testing their patience and endurance beneath the surface before he grants them communion with aquatic forms.

npc:devrak.text: Devrak. At the Crossroads, Devrak keeps the Horde’s wind riders ready for the roads across Kalimdor. The orc flight master carries couriers and supplies between Durotar, Mulgore, frontier outposts, and the Horde’s capitals. At the Crossroads, Devrak tends the wind riders that link the Horde’s far-flung holdings. The outpost stands where Kalimdor’s major trade routes meet, exposed beneath the sun and vulnerable to quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Quick flights matter here. Devrak pairs seasoned travelers and new messengers with trained wind riders that cross the savannah and reach Mulgore’s mountains or Durotar’s stone canyons. Devrak also helps move supplies from the frontier. Barrens hunters bring in meat and pelts, and he helps send them to Orgrimmar’s cooking fires and Thunder Bluff’s tanners. He introduces new couriers to flight masters across the continents, keeping an aerial route open to the Horde’s heartlands. Devrak tends more than beasts at the Crossroads. When the settlement comes under attack, he calls enraged wyverns to strike intruders with venomous stingers and talons. His roost is a dangerous target for anyone who attacks.

npc:eitrigg.text: Eitrigg. In Orgrimmar, Eitrigg stands beside Warchief Thrall as a trusted advisor. A veteran of the First and Second Wars, he left the Blackrock clan’s Horde after its defeat and lived in exile. Now he helps Thrall guide the New Horde toward honor and shamanism. Born on Draenor among the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg fought for the Horde in the First and Second Wars. The battles and the Horde’s defeat in the second war forced him to face how far his people had fallen into bloodlust and demonic corruption. Sickened by what the Horde had become, he left its scattered remnants and sought solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron. During his exile, Eitrigg sheltered in an abandoned tower near Hearthglen. The human paladin Tirion Fordring found him, and their clash brought the tower’s ruins down around them. Eitrigg pulled the unconscious human to safety instead of finishing him. Moved by this act of martial honor, Tirion swore friendship and kept the hermit’s location secret. The local Alliance authorities eventually captured Eitrigg and sentenced him to hang in Stratholme. Tirion cast aside his knighthood, lands, and freedom to attack the city and rescue him. Their bond showed both warriors that honor could cross the hatred between their peoples. In Stratholme, Thrall’s newly united Horde raided the city during Tirion’s attempt to free Eitrigg and carried the aging warrior away. Meeting Thrall convinced Eitrigg that the orcs were casting off demonic corruption and returning to their ancestral shamanic heritage. He crossed the Great Sea with Thrall to Kalimdor and took a revered place in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Wisdom. Now Eitrigg advises the young Warchief inside Grommash Hold. He helps evaluate new recruits and shares the wisdom he earned, so the New Horde does not repeat the tragedies of the past.

npc:executor-arren.text: Executor Arren. At Deathknell, Executor Arren rallies the settlement's defense as undead rise from their graves. He leads the fight against Scourge zombies, wild beasts, and threats to the Forsaken. Executor Arren directs Deathknell's defense from outside the chapel. In the crypts, caretakers guide the newly risen through their confusion. Arren turns their thoughts to surviving beyond the graves. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes the effort to clear mindless zombies from the village borders. Here, in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall, the Forsaken hold their ground. Beyond the confused newly risen, danger surrounds Deathknell. Under Arren's orders, scouts and initiates strike at vicious spiders in Night Web's Hollow and hunt predators along the woodland edges. He calls every capable hand to act. Their work tests whether new arrivals can defend their second chance and serve the Dark Lady.

npc:executor-zygand.text: Executor Zygand. In Brill, Executor Zygand directs the Forsaken defenses across central Tirisfal Glades. He reports to the Undercity's high command and coordinates the fight against Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken lands. After the Forsaken awakened in Deathknell, Executor Zygand took charge of regional defenses from Brill. Officers such as Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea report to him. Zygand gathers scouts' reports and sends able recruits to guard Lordaeron's borders against encroachment. The Scarlet Crusade's presence across Tirisfal Glades keeps Executor Zygand busy. He sends agents against Crusader scouts, encampments, and forward bases. That work keeps the zealots from gathering enough strength to threaten the approaches to the Undercity.

npc:gan-rul-bloodeye.text: Gan'rul Bloodeye. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye trains warlocks beneath the city. In the Cleft of Shadow, Horde initiates learn darker demonic rites and how to bend voidwalkers and succubi to their will. Warlocks study out of sight in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. Warchief Thrall tolerates them in the new Horde, though Durotar's open sunlight is no place for their dark arts. The cavern gives shadow weavers, rogues, and fel casters room to study unmolested. From there, Gan'rul teaches rising practitioners of fel magic. Ambitious warlocks come to Gan'rul to learn dangerous summoning rites. Those seeking to bind a greater demon, such as a resilient voidwalker or a seductive succubus, must secure ritual components and learn the precise incantations. The summoned creature must be dominated before it consumes its master.

npc:gann-stonespire.text: Gann Stonespire. Along the southern Barrens road near Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire seeks retaliation for his people’s displacement. The tauren nomad’s tribe hunted on land now occupied by a dwarven excavation. Gann Stonespire camps beside the southern Barrens road after the dwarven expedition arrived from Ironforge and built Bael Modan. The surrounding land had been his tribe’s ancestral territory and hunting grounds. Dwarven miners drove the tauren from their soil with pickaxes, firearms, and heavy machinery, and refused peaceful overtures. Gann will not surrender his heritage quietly. He calls on travelers to strike back at the excavators.

npc:gazrog.text: Gazrog. At the Crossroads, Gazrog keeps watch over the Horde’s roads and supply lines. He calls on passing Horde travelers to face threats in the Barrens and search for lost patrols. Gazrog watches over the Crossroads and the roads beyond it. Marauders and beasts threaten the supplies moving through this isolated settlement, so he works with its defenders to keep cargo, coin, and couriers moving. The wilderness demands constant attention, and Gazrog depends on passing travelers to answer trouble beyond the outpost’s stockades. Gazrog’s watch extends across trails where raptors prey on travelers and quilboar clans ambush scouts. He coordinates responses to highway robberies, including the recovery of stolen Horde shipments. He also keeps track of missing soldiers, among them the grunt Dogran, who is injured and held by the quilboar.

npc:gornek.text: Gornek. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek oversees new orc and Darkspear troll recruits in Durotar. He receives those preparing to prove their worth to the New Horde. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek puts new Horde recruits through their first test of discipline. Warchief Thrall's order is clear: every youth and newcomer must earn a place through grit and perseverance. Gornek assesses those entering the valley, reads their introductory orders, and directs them to trainers around the compound. Whether an initiate carries an encrypted scrawl, a glyphic parchment, or a simple tablet, Gornek receives the credentials and sends them onto a harsh path of survival. The valley's arid canyons test battle skill and teach the New Horde's communal ways. Gornek keeps novices from lingering aimlessly, pointing them toward nearby scorpid burrows, feral boar dens, and veteran instructors. Those who survive the training grounds and slay the threats in the red rock gullies receive Gornek's final acknowledgment before he sends them out into Durotar's wider, perilous landscape.

npc:gunther-arcanus.text:
Gunther Arcanus. On an island in Brightwater Lake, Gunther Arcanus keeps apart from others after escaping the Lich King's control. He believes every other undead remains a Scourge thrall. During the Third War, the Scourge swept across the north. The Plague of Undeath killed Gunther and raised him to serve. His mastery of the arcane and iron will let him break the Lich King's mental hold alone. He needed neither the Lich King's weakening nor Lady Sylvanas's help, as others did.

Believing every other walking corpse remained a mindless Scourge thrall, Gunther withdrew to an island in Tirisfal Glades. Shambling guardians surround him. He has cut off all contact with the living and the dead alike.

npc:high-executor-hadrec.text: High Executor Hadrec. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec directs the Forsaken garrison across Silverpine Forest. He oversees defense against threats such as the Rot Hide gnolls and investigates scouts missing across the zone. High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken military operations from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. The Dark Lady’s forces hold Tirisfal Glades, but Silverpine faces hostile Dalaran mages, feral worgen, and encroaching gnolls. Hadrec must strengthen Forsaken control and suppress threats to Undercity authority south of the capital. The Rot Hide gnolls and Fenris Isle occupy much of Hadrec’s attention. Tainted by undeath, the beasts have overrun the Dead Fields and the shores of Lake Lordamere, threatening Forsaken patrols. Hadrec sends agents to search ruined ferries and farmsteads for clues, learn what empowers the gnolls, and prepare a strike against their island stronghold.

npc:islen-waterseer.text: Islen Waterseer. Beside the Tidus Stair, respected tauren shaman Islen Waterseer guides Horde initiates through the trials of water. She lives by a quiet fishing hut and teaches shamans to attune to water spirits as they seek their Water Totem. On the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer keeps to the craggy Tidus Stair, where arid plains meet the Great Sea. Water spirits are raw and near along this shore. Islen chooses this quiet outpost over thunderous halls and busy cities, spending her days listening to the tides. Shamans seeking communion with water come to her for guidance. To know water, a shaman needs inner harmony and spiritual sight as well as study. Islen guides seekers in preparing the Water Sapta, a sacred brew that pierces the veil between mortal senses and elemental manifestations. She teaches that water can be unyielding and deep, yet fluid and restorative. Anyone who calls on its aid must show it great respect. Though Islen lives quietly on the coast, her spiritual ties reach across Kalimdor. She shares a close, enduring friendship with Greta Mosshoof, another wise tauren skilled in the restorative arts. Islen's knowledge of water's purifying nature reaches beyond the Barrens, bringing spiritual aid to lands afflicted by deep corruption.

npc:kadrak.text: Kadrak. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the northern frontier between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He directs dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest, where the Horde fights the night elves. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the main route between the Barrens and Ashenvale. The barricade marks a hard border: Horde-held plains lie to the south, and night elf-guarded woods stretch north. Kadrak keeps watch against Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures, holding the perimeter against incursions. Kadrak also handles military reports between the Barrens and logging camps deeper in Ashenvale. Couriers bring him combat reports from the Warsong Outriders, and he directs supplies and reinforcements to outposts such as Splintertree Post. Those who report to Kadrak are sent onward into the struggle for the forest.

npc:magatha-grimtotem.text: Magatha Grimtotem. On Elder Rise, Magatha Grimtotem presses her challenge to Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren. The Grimtotem matriarch and Thunder Bluff's Elder Crone is a formidable shaman and political schemer. Magatha Grimtotem leads the Grimtotem tribe from Elder Rise, with her own retinue and bodyguards. An arranged union brought her authority, then her mate died in a climbing accident. Her reclusive tribe follows her as its political and spiritual leader. Magatha preaches tauren dominance, against Cairne Bloodhoof's vision. She sees other mortal races as intruders on Kalimdor, to be eradicated or swept aside. Though Magatha openly disdains other races, she was among the first to argue that the Forsaken should join the Horde. She says the tauren can teach the undead spiritual balance and help them reclaim their humanity. Beneath Thunder Bluff, she also works directly with the Royal Apothecary Society. There she consults figures such as Apothecary Zamah about practical alchemy and arcane relics.

npc:magistrate-sevren.text: Magistrate Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren directs the settlement’s defense and sends newcomers to steady the lands around the Undercity. From Brill’s town hall, Magistrate Sevren directs civil and strategic affairs north of the Undercity. New Forsaken arrive in Tirisfal Glades to find local troubles waiting. Sevren sends them to restore order, secure ruined places, and suppress threats in the surrounding hills. The dead of Tirisfal and their burial grounds are chief concerns for Magistrate Sevren. Scourge-aligned Rot Hide gnolls, graverobbers, and rogue undead threaten the graves and Sylvanas Windrunner’s growing dominion. Sevren seeks to reclaim ancestral tombs such as the Agamand Family Crypt. He also keeps deserters and uncooperative forces from undermining Forsaken authority.

npc:mangletooth.text: Mangletooth. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth faces execution in a Horde cage and bargains with those who visit him. He offers knowledge of his rivals and Agamaggan's ancient lore in return for their help. Tauren hunters and orc sentries keep Mangletooth in a cage at Camp Taurajo. The captured Razormane quilboar awaits execution, but he still tries to sway his captors and visiting Horde adventurers. He urges them to strike at the enemies of his tribe, hoping to prove his worth or win his freedom. Mangletooth knows the religious history of his people. During the ancient War of the Ancients, Agamaggan's spilled blood gave rise to the Barrens' massive thorns. Mangletooth gathers red crystalline Blood Shards from fallen Bristlebacks and channels the lingering divine power within them, granting ancient blessings to those who help him.

npc:master-apothecary-faranell.text: Master Apothecary Faranell. In the Undercity, Faranell directs the Royal Apothecary Society from the depths of the Apothecarium. Once a respected Dalaran scholar, he now leads the Forsaken’s search for a New Plague to destroy the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell spent decades studying alchemy beside Dalaran’s learned mages. In life, he sought cures, remedies, and potions to better mortal health. The Scourge plague killed him, but he rose again as a free-willed Forsaken. His curiosity turned cruel, and healing salves gave way to catastrophic reagents. His vast knowledge made him one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner’s most valued researchers in the depths of Lordaeron’s fallen capital. From the Apothecarium, Faranell directs the Royal Apothecary Society’s far-reaching research. He oversees the making of lumbering abominations and guides apothecaries stationed throughout Lordaeron and beyond. Field researchers gather strange venom, tainted blood, and cursed flora across the continents. Each batch goes into his vats for distillation and refinement.

npc:master-gadrin.text: Master Gadrin. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin guides the Darkspear through exile and loss. The elder witch doctor once trained the tribe's priests and mages with Zalazane. Now he helps his people and seeks to break the dark curse over their home on the Echo Isles. Before the Darkspear reached Kalimdor, Master Gadrin guided generations of his people in the South Seas. He served as a witch doctor on the islands they called home, teaching the tribe's mystical ways. On the Echo Isles, Master Gadrin and the young witch doctor Zalazane trained the tribe's priests and mages together. Zalazane fell under the pull of the dark voodoo he sought to wield, and madness took hold. He enslaved the minds of his people and drove Vol'jin and the uncorrupted Darkspear onto the mainland of Durotar. Now in Sen'jin Village, Gadrin bears the grief of watching a companion become a tyrant. He works to lay slain tribesfolk to rest and end Zalazane's rule. Master Gadrin knows more of troll spiritualism and loa lore than almost anyone alive in the Horde. Scholars, shamans, and the Royal Apothecary Society seek his counsel on arcane and alchemical mysteries. When the Burning Blade threatens Durotar, or distant researchers need forgotten rites, Gadrin draws on what he knows. He can decipher the ancient tablets of Zul'Farrak and invoke Shadra the spider loa, then craft the bindings such a rite requires.

npc:mebok-mizzyrix.text: Mebok Mizzyrix. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix hires travelers to gather strange finds across the Barrens and beyond. This goblin entrepreneur hopes to turn unusual plants and creatures into profit. His best-known venture is a drink made with raptor horns, meant to sharpen the mind. Mebok Mizzyrix works from Ratchet, a neutral port where sailors, pirates and merchants meet. He carries the Steamwheedle spirit of seizing every chance for profit. Rather than deal in ore or cloth, he seeks rare creatures and plants from Kalimdor’s wilds. He believes they can be made into valuable brews and goods. Mebok’s chief venture is a drink he hopes will boost the drinker’s intellect. He believes the cunning and ferocity of local raptors come from the horns on their snouts. So he hires hunters to bring him whole horns from across the Barrens. Ethics and taste matter less to him than the chance to sell a brew customers believe works. Mebok also seeks strange specimens beyond raptor horns. He wants volatile Deepmoss spider eggs and rare Blueleaf tubers buried in the brambles of Razorfen Kraul. These commissions send mercenaries into dangerous country. Mebok believes any creature or plant with strange properties can be bottled and sold.

npc:melor-stonehoof.text: Melor Stonehoof. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof sends Horde hunters to face dangerous beasts. Their trials across the Barrens and Thousand Needles test tracking and mettle. From Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof watches the plains. To the tauren, hunting joins survival with spiritual balance and respect for nature’s greatest predators. He teaches Horde bowmen and bladesmen to honor that balance, sending promising stalkers to test their craft against legendary beasts. Melor sends hunters after elusive beasts that threaten the wilds. In the Barrens, they aid Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. Then they pursue Steelsnap, a cunning and vicious hyena in Thousand Needles. These trials show whether hunters can outsmart and outfight central Kalimdor’s deadliest creatures. Those who prove their skill in the Barrens face beasts in distant lands. Melor sends seasoned hunters after Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk in the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh, and Frostmaw, a savage yeti in the Alterac Mountains. Each hunt tests whether a stalker has mastered the Hunter’s Way.

npc:menara-voidrender.text: Menara Voidrender. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender teaches warlocks from both factions the dark arts. The human warlock shares her knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft from a refuge in Kalimdor, far from orthodox authorities. Menara Voidrender works from Ratchet, the neutral goblin port in the Barrens. Many warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms study in cellars or hidden slaughterhouses beneath their cities, but Ratchet keeps Menara away from the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, and Orgrimmar's overseers. There, she can pursue occult studies in plain sight. She teaches any capable apprentice, whatever their faction, making her a rare meeting point for practitioners of the dark arts. Veteran conjurers know Menara as an authority on orbs that imprison and harness demonic spirits. She works with intricate reagents and guides apprentices through demanding rituals to make enchanted attire and binding implements. Her skill is known as far as Ironforge and the Undercity, and senior warlocks across Azeroth send their most promising students across the sea to seek her counsel.

npc:morin-cloudstalker.text: Morin Cloudstalker. Along the eastern road from Bloodhoof Village, Morin Cloudstalker keeps watch over Mulgore. The tauren scout follows trade routes and investigates dangers to travelers. Morin Cloudstalker watches the trail east toward the Barrens. He scouts the road and guards travelers crossing Mulgore. The plains are usually peaceful, but shifting territories and busy trade routes have brought opportunists and bandits near the tauren homeland. Morin's scouts attacked and burned a Venture Co. caravan on Stonebull Lake's northern shore. Goblin salvagers soon appeared by the wagons. So Morin sent adventurers to inspect the surviving supply crates and learn what the Venture Co. had been hauling.

npc:mull-thunderhorn.text: Mull Thunderhorn. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn keeps Mulgore’s sacred wells and the land’s balance. He serves the Earth Mother and guides young tauren as outside exploitation threatens the ancestral springs. From Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn watches over Mulgore’s spiritual well-being. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to make a permanent home, but greed and reckless expansion already threaten their lands. So Mull guides young braves setting out from Camp Narache and calls on them to guard their ancestors’ vital resources.

npc:orgnil-soulscar.text: Orgnil Soulscar. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar watches for threats within Durotar. He gathers intelligence and coordinates defenses against dangers to the young orc nation, especially the Burning Blade cult in the canyons. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar tracks hidden threats across Durotar. While grunt patrols watch for Alliance forces and centaur raiders, he looks for danger among the orcs themselves. Scouts bring him reports from across the region, and he searches them for signs of corrupt rituals and secret gatherings.

npc:shadow-priest-allister.text:
Shadow Priest Allister. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister directs the Forsaken's efforts across Silverpine Forest. He watches nearby threats and guards Lordaeron's borders for the Dark Lady. Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken scouts from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From there, he watches for renegade humans and beasts. He also tracks arcane activity around Dalaran. Allister's chief concern is Dalaran's surviving mages. He watches especially closely those at Ambermill, who probe across the borders. He will not let the Kirin Tor gain a foothold in Forsaken lands. His agents intercept messengers, decipher arcane runes, and seek the wizards' long-term aims. Allister's duties as a strategist share his attention with the study of shadow. He wrote 'Holy Bologna: What the Light Won't Tell You', a sharp attack on traditional holy doctrine. The book considers undeath's harsh realities and the Holy Light's failure to aid those cast aside by life.

Somehow, copies have reached the ruins of Dire Maul in Kalimdor.

npc:shadow-priest-sarvis.text: Shadow Priest Sarvis. In Deathknell's ruined chapel, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives the newly awakened Forsaken purpose and direction. In Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis guides Forsaken who have just risen from their graves. The awakening can be harsh and frightening. Some lose their minds to frenzy or despair, so Sarvis gives the newly risen a purpose. He sends them to put down the mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and guard Deathknell's borders against the Scourge. Shadow Priest Sarvis directs Deathknell's defenses against threats in Tirisfal Glades. Scourge forces test the town's perimeter, so Sarvis sends novices to gather vital intelligence and face trials of arms. The Forsaken must hold Deathknell against those forces.

npc:shael-dryn.text: Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. She serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Stationed beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn keeps watch alongside the night elf sentinels guarding the eastern approaches of the forest. When corruption surfaces among the local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, her deep natural understanding allows her to guide adventurers through the steps required to restore spiritual balance.

npc:shenthul.text: Shenthul. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul trains rogues and serves the Shattered Hand. He directs covert work across Kalimdor and brings promising rogues into its ranks. Shenthul trains rogues in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. While warriors and shamans march openly across Durotar, he teaches stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. His students learn fieldcraft and lethal arts for work in Kalimdor's harsh wilderness and unforgiving politics. Shenthul speaks for the Shattered Hand, once an orcish clan and now the Horde's intelligence network and secret service. He describes it as a watchful presence across Kalimdor, investigating, judging, and carrying out its own sentences. Pragmatic and independent of shifting politics, Shenthul reminds outsiders that the Shattered Hand existed before Warchief Thrall took power and will endure after him.

npc:sputtervalve.text: Sputtervalve. Under pressure in Ratchet, Sputtervalve races to finish shredder research for the Tinkers' Union. Director Riddlevox holds him to crushing deadlines, and he hires adventurers to steal designs from the rival Venture Company. In Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. The goblin engineer oversees shredder development and has found the work brutal. Modern mechanization moves fast, the Venture Company presses hard, and his own prototypes are few. With the deadline closing in, Sputtervalve fears admitting failure to the Union. He turns to a familiar goblin practice: stealing better designs from those who built them first. The Venture Company's drilling operation at the Sludge Fen, to the northwest, is Sputtervalve's chief target. Its latest shredders have interchangeable hands, refined control grips, and advanced inner workings, including the elusive samophlange. Sputtervalve sent his associate Wizzlecrank into the Fen for field research, but Wizzlecrank became trapped. Now Sputtervalve hires wandering mercenaries to recover the stolen technology and rescue his partner. Sputtervalve also helps with strange curiosities that pass through the Barrens. Adventurers sometimes bring him bizarre artifacts infused with corruption from the Wailing Caverns, such as a glowing shard. He knows the local landscape well enough to point them away from machinery and toward the isolated druids encamped above the caverns.

npc:strahad-farsan.text: Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan teaches warlocks to bind demons. The human warlock lives in a stone tower in the Barrens, beyond the reach of ordinary Alliance and Horde politics. Students of fel magic come from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity to learn from him. Strahad Farsan keeps to a stone tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. The goblin port's neutral ground lets him practice dangerous summonings away from Alliance magistrates and Horde shamans. His acolytes gather around him as he studies the Twisting Nether, apart from the struggles over territory below. Strahad learned the danger of demonic binding firsthand. His first attempt to bind a felhunter nearly cost him his life, leaving him cautious and exacting. Despite being human, he has earned the respect of Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind and demonic scholars in the Undercity and Orgrimmar. Warlocks of either faction seeking to command felhunters or fiery steeds are sent to his tower.

npc:sylvanas-windrunner.text:
Sylvanas Windrunner. Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, Sylvanas Windrunner rules the Forsaken from the Undercity. Once Silvermoon's Ranger-General, she was slain and raised by Arthas Menethil, then broke free of the Lich King's control. She joined Thrall's Horde to secure her people's future and seeks vengeance on the Scourge. Sylvanas Windrunner commanded Quel'Thalas's defense as Silvermoon's Ranger-General. When Prince Arthas Menethil led the Scourge into the high elven kingdom for the Sunwell, she fought to stop him. Angered by her resistance, Arthas murdered her and denied her a clean death. He tore her soul from her body and made her a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and help slaughter her own people. After the Third War, the Lich King's weakening grip freed Sylvanas, and she reclaimed her preserved body. She gathered other undead who had regained their free will, then drove the dreadlords from Lordaeron's ruins. She named her people the Forsaken and made the Undercity their realm beneath the ruins.

The Forsaken faced Scourge remnants, zealous Scarlet crusaders, and wary human realms. They needed allies, so Sylvanas made an uneasy alliance with Warchief Thrall and the Horde.

npc:telf-joolam.text: Telf Joolam. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, Telf Joolam guides Horde initiates through the trials of fire. The Darkspear shaman teaches them to commune with and command the volatile element. Telf Joolam tends the Shrine of the Dormant Flame among the crags overlooking the borderlands. Fire spirits demand sharp discipline and unwavering focus, unlike the calm certainty of earth or the patient depth of water. Telf prepares young shamans for trials that test their worth before the wild embers consume them. Under Telf's direction, initiates brew and drink a ritual Fire Sapta, opening their mortal eyes to the unseen elemental planes. He sends them up the rocky summits to face burning spirits. Those who earn the flame must respect its ravenous hunger and resist reckless pride.

npc:thork.text: Thork. At the Crossroads, Thork keeps watch over the settlement’s defenses. He sends Horde adventurers against raiders and works to keep supply routes open. Thork commands the defenses at the Crossroads, where roads link Durotar, Mulgore, and lands beyond. The town faces threats from every side. Quilboar raids, centaur attacks, and harpies on the prowl stretch his forces thin. Thork calls on capable travelers to meet dangers his guards cannot handle alone. Thork’s watch reaches beyond the Crossroads walls. He sends scouts and messengers north to the Mor’shan Rampart, where they report to Kadrak. The northern and eastern routes carry supplies through the Barrens. Keeping those roads open sustains the Horde’s presence across the scrublands.

npc:thotar.text: Thotar. In Razor Hill, Thotar teaches young Horde hunters the ways of tracking and taming beasts. He trains orcs and trolls who have left the Valley of Trials to face Durotar’s wildlife. In Razor Hill, Thotar trains Horde hunters for the wilderness of Durotar. New recruits learn the basics in the Valley of Trials, then come to him as they face more dangerous predators. He teaches marksmanship and the respect needed to live alongside and direct Kalimdor’s deadliest creatures, drawing on traditions passed down through generations of orcs. Thotar guides young hunters through the ancient art of taming beasts. He sends them into arid canyons to calm and bond with native creatures, including venomous scorpids, armored surf crawlers, and cunning boars. His instruction teaches Horde trackers to build a bond with nature rather than rely on force.

npc:thrall.text: Thrall. Thrall now rules from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar, Warchief of the Horde and ruler of Durotar. Once a human slave raised as an arena fighter, he freed his people, restored their shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to a new homeland. Thrall was born Go'el, son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka. Gul'dan's assassins murdered his parents when he was an infant, and human commander Aedelas Blackmoore found him and named him Thrall, meaning slave. At Durnholde Keep, Blackmoore raised him as an arena fighter and taught him human tactics. With help from his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped. The Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar guided him away from demonic corruption and taught him to master the elemental spirits. Thrall became the first orcish shaman of a new generation. After the Second War, Thrall joined Orgrim Doomhammer to free the orcs languishing in Alliance internment camps. Doomhammer fell in battle and passed his black plate armor and mighty warhammer to Thrall, naming him Warchief. The mysterious Prophet Medivh brought prophetic visions, and Thrall led his people aboard captured human ships across the Great Sea. They reached Kalimdor and escaped the doom falling upon the Eastern Kingdoms. In Kalimdor, Thrall reshaped the Horde from a warmongering force into an alliance built on survival and honor. He rescued Vol'jin's Darkspear trolls and allied with Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren. With human and night elf forces, the coalition defeated the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal. Thrall then founded Durotar and its capital, Orgrimmar, named for his father and mentor. He keeps an uneasy peace with Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore while defending his fragile nation and weighing controversial alliances, including the Forsaken of Lordaeron.

npc:tonga-runetotem.text: Tonga Runetotem. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem watches the Barrens' oases grow sick. Sent from Thunder Bluff, the tauren druid studies a corruption harming the region's wildlife and seeks its source before the fragile ecosystem fails. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies the Barrens' changing land. His elders in Thunder Bluff sent him from Mulgore, and he knows the dry savannah well. Where travelers see scrub and predators, Tonga watches for signs of the land's health. Lately, those signs have turned troubling. He seeks travelers who can help him investigate the scattered oases, the heart of life across the savannah. Tonga bears the Runetotem clan name and the druidic heritage championed by Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. Hamuul keeps ties with the Cenarion Circle and studies in Moonglade's sacred groves, while scouts like Tonga serve on the frontier. Tonga draws on Moonglade's botanical wisdom to prepare healing salves and counter poisons. His work puts the young tauren druidic tradition to use within the fledgling Horde.

npc:turak-runetotem.text:
Turak Runetotem. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem guides young tauren toward nature and balance. From the Hall of Elders on Elder Rise, he assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem and leads novices through trials to commune with spirits and master animal forms. In the Hall of Elders atop Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise, Turak Runetotem guides those who seek the druid’s path. He assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in bringing the ancient druidic arts back among the tauren. Turak teaches that a druid honors the Earthmother’s will. Strength of body must rest upon spiritual respect and harmony with nature. When fledgling druids are ready for animal forms, Turak sends them into the wider world. He teaches them to join the Cenarion Circle and travel by teleportation across Kalimdor to Moonglade. Turak remembers his own first communion with the Great Bear Spirit as bewildering and intense. To test his students’ courage, he sends them to face Lunaclaw and win the strength of body and heart required for the Path of the Claw. Turak teaches more than the primal forms of combat. He sends his disciples to Dendrite Starblaze to study poison, and Dendrite sends them to help animals poisoned near the Crossroads. Even Turak is surprised by the rash of poisonings.

Turak also guides novices through arduous rites beneath the tides, where they awaken their aquatic form. These trials shape them into protectors able to heal Azeroth’s deepest wounds.

npc:varimathras.text:
Varimathras. In the Royal Quarter, Varimathras advises Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and commands her forces. After defeat in Lordaeron's civil war, he pledged himself to the Banshee Queen and now serves at her right hand. Before the Third War, Kil'jaeden sent Varimathras and his fellow dreadlords to guard the Lich King. They were to ensure Ner'zhul's spirit served the Legion's plans. With his brothers Detheroc and Balnazzar, Varimathras oversaw the Scourge in Lordaeron while Archimonde invaded Kalimdor.

The Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, but the three dreadlords stayed entrenched in the Capital City's ruins. They learned of their master's defeat only when Prince Arthas returned and drove them into hiding. As the Lich King's hold over his undead weakened, Varimathras tried to make the newly freed banshee Sylvanas Windrunner serve the dreadlords' new regime. Sylvanas refused and rallied liberated undead to destroy his outpost. Facing execution, Varimathras begged for his life and offered tactical secrets, including knowledge of his brothers' fortifications. Sylvanas spared him and bound him to her service as a weapon against his kin.

npc:vol-jin.text: Vol'jin. In Orgrimmar, Vol'jin advises Warchief Thrall while seeking a lasting home for his people. The Darkspear chieftain is a master shadow hunter. Vol'jin leads the Darkspear after his father, Sen'jin, dies on their ancestral island. Sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroy the isolated tribe, but Thrall's orcs intervene and forge a deep bond with the trolls. After fleeing the ruined islands, Vol'jin pledges his people to the New Horde and brings them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. The Darkspear settle in Durotar, but Zalazane's betrayal on the Echo Isles drives many refugees to the mainland at Sen'jin Village. Vol'jin spends much of his time in Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, giving Thrall his strategic counsel and shadow hunter skill. From the orcish capital, he watches over the young Horde and works to reclaim his people's lands.

npc:yaw-sharpmane.text: Yaw Sharpmane. Bloodhoof Village is where Yaw Sharpmane teaches young tauren hunters. He shows them how to track, survive, and tame Mulgore's wild beasts. Yaw Sharpmane teaches marksmanship, tracking, and survival in Bloodhoof Village. Young hunters who have proven themselves in Red Cloud Mesa come to him to hone their skills before they venture onto Mulgore's wider plains. Yaw Sharpmane guides new hunters through the ancient rite of taming wild beasts. He asks them to bond with Mulgore's native animals, testing their patience and respect for nature's balance. Then he teaches them to care for and train a lasting companion.

subzone:agama-gor.text: Agama'gor. Agama'gor stands north of the road from Camp Taurajo toward Mulgore. Bristleback quilboar hold this encampment in the southern Barrens, keeping pressure on the nearby Horde outpost. Agama'gor is a Bristleback stronghold in the southern Barrens. Its huts, brambles, and crude totems lie close to Camp Taurajo. The quilboar threaten travelers moving between the Barrens and Mulgore’s grassy hills, and Horde scouts and hunters fight to contain them. Bristleback quilboar in Agama'gor carry crimson stones called Blood Shards. Mangletooth, an exiled quilboar held captive at Camp Taurajo, seeks these stones because of ancient beliefs about Agamaggan’s sacred essence. Horde adventurers raid the encampment for shards and trade them to Mangletooth for tribal charms.

subzone:agamand-family-crypt.text:
Agamand Family Crypt. The Scourge has seized the Agamand Family Crypt just north of Agamand Mills. Once the resting place of Tirisfal's wealthy farming dynasty, its tombs now hold ancestors raised by Captain Dargol as mindless terrors. The Agamand family once held broad estates across northern Tirisfal Glades. Their ancestors rest in a hillside crypt, until the Plague ruined the kingdom and Captain Dargol seized the tombs for the Scourge.

Through dark necromancy, Dargol awakened the Agamand dead as vengeful skeletons and apparitions. Their restless forms make the family burial ground a Scourge foothold beside Forsaken territory.

subzone:agamand-mills.text:
Agamand Mills. Across northern Tirisfal, Agamand Mills now shelter the Scourge’s strongest hold in the region. The wealthy Agamand dynasty once ruled this farm and milling estate. The Agamand family built an estate around a vast network of mills in northern Tirisfal. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron during the Third War, patriarch Gregor Agamand refused to flee. He fortified the compound and persuaded retainers and laborers to stand with him. Their stores and stone walls might have held, but their youngest son, Devlin Agamand, betrayed them.

Devlin slaughtered the watchmen and let the walking dead into the sleeping quarters. The defenders were crippled from within before they fell. The family joined the mindless ranks of the undead. Agamand Mills are the Scourge’s strongest hold in Tirisfal Glades and a direct threat to the Forsaken realm. Rotting windmills turn above fields crawling with wights, zombies, and skeletal horrors. Beneath the estate, Captain Dargol commands the garrison from the Agamand Family Crypt. There he practices necromancy, reanimating generations of Agamand ancestors.

From Brill, Magistrate Sevren and the Deathguards fight to clear the mills and purge the Scourge before it can march on the Undercity.

subzone:ambermill.text: Ambermill. In southeastern Silverpine Forest, Ambermill's wizards hold a fortified outpost southwest of Lordamere Lake. Once a quiet lumber village, it now shelters surviving wizards and apprentices from Dalaran as they resist the Forsaken to the south. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town. After Lordaeron fell, surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor moved in and fortified it. Now Dalaran spellscribes, conjurors, and apprentices patrol its buildings and stables. They hold this forward redoubt against the undead.

subzone:apothecarium.text: Apothecarium. In the Undercity’s southwest quarter, the Apothecarium drives the Royal Apothecary Society’s work. Under Master Apothecary Faranell, Forsaken alchemists pursue plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors for Lady Sylvanas’s campaign against the living and the Scourge. Vats, dissection tables, and chemical fumes fill the Apothecarium’s southwestern terrace. Master Apothecary Faranell leads the Royal Apothecary Society’s work there, studying mortality and rot. Alchemists and surgeons experiment with tissue grafts and vivisection, then assemble mighty abominations. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has charged them with making a plague to eradicate both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron. Alchemists and herbalists come to this quarter from across the Horde in the Eastern Kingdoms. Initiates and masters gather beside toxic canals to distill concoctions and study botanical blights. They also seek counsel from master practitioners.

subzone:bael-dun-digsite.text: Bael'dun Digsite. Dwarven prospectors dig into the western hills of Mulgore at Bael'dun Digsite. Their search for ancient Titan relics has brought them against the tauren, who see the work as an insult to the Earth Mother. Dwarven prospectors cut into the mountain slopes of western Mulgore. Their camp marks the southernmost reach of the Explorers' League expedition based at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. They seek ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains, bringing picks, shovels, and blasting powder. They heed neither borders nor the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes. The Bloodhoof tribe sees the digging as an assault on the Earth Mother. Baine Bloodhoof urged caution and warned the dwarves to leave, but they would not abandon their trenches. With diplomacy failed, the tauren resolved to break the expedition's tools and drive out the miners before their work cuts deeper into Mulgore's sacred earth.

subzone:bael-dun-keep.text: Bael'dun Keep. Dwarven forces hold Bael'dun Keep above the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under General Twinbraid, this imposing fortification anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region and brings it into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Bael'dun Keep rises over the Bael Modan excavation as the fortified military heart of Ironforge's presence in the southern Barrens. Dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder designed the stronghold to protect the Prospectors and archaeologists searching the trenches for ancient titan artifacts. Ironworks and artillery arm its garrison, which keeps a vigilant watch, secures dwarven supply lines, and projects Alliance military power into Kalimdor's heartland. The keep and its adjoining digsite displaced the local Stonespire tribe of tauren from their ancestral home. Bael'dun remains a flashpoint in the Barrens, and nearby Horde outposts see it as a flagrant military intrusion. Gann Stonespire wages a personal war of vengeance against the invaders. Aggrieved tauren, opportunistic scouts, and suspicious outposts such as Camp Taurajo keep the fortress under threat of raids and sabotage.

subzone:bael-modan.text: Bael Modan. Dwarven crews blast into the red earth at Bael Modan, searching for Titan relics. Their fortified outpost has driven the Stonespire tauren from their sacred land and kindled a bitter fight. Bael Modan's walls guard Bael'dun Keep, siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors came to Kalimdor convinced an ancient Titan facility lay beneath the red earth. Their blasting tore through sacred ground of the Stonespire tauren. The expedition answered no call to negotiate. Gunfire and explosives drove the tribe from its ancestral lands, leaving survivors scattered and vengeful.

subzone:balnir-farmstead.text: Balnir Farmstead. In eastern Tirisfal, Balnir Farmstead lies ruined just behind the Bulwark. Once worked by the Balnir family, the estate now draws Scourge slipping past the defenses. Snapdragons still bloom in the garden where the Balnir family worked their homestead for generations. During the Third War, the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and overran the farm. Its people were lost, and the buildings now rot among eastern Tirisfal’s hills. Mindless Scourge slip past the Bulwark and gather among the farmstead’s ruins. Forsaken deathguards watch the grounds warily. Meanwhile, Undercity magi gather surviving snapdragons from the garden to learn how deeply plague corruption has reached into the soil.

subzone:bandarion-keep.text: Bandarion Keep. At Bandarion Keep, defenders watch the coast and the woodland for danger. Near the Whispering Forest, the outpost bears Garek Bandarion’s name and is bound to Tyr's Watch. Bandarion Keep guards western Tirisfal Glades near the Whispering Forest. Named for Garek Bandarion, the stronghold is closely bound to Tyr's Watch. Quartermaster Jorin Croge works to keep the garrison supplied. Yet the keep lies far from the courtyards of the Undercity. Threats press Bandarion Keep from several directions. Vile Fin murlocs raid the nearby waters, while the Scarlet Crusade tests the defenders in skirmishes. Mindless Scourge thralls wander through the gloom. Some paladins have struggled to accept their unlife as Forsaken and have fallen to madness. They turn their weapons against their own kindred.

subzone:beren-s-peril.text:
Beren's Peril. At Beren's Peril, Scourge loyal to Thule Ravenclaw gather in the hills southwest of Ambermill and threaten the Forsaken. High in the crags southwest of Ambermill, a cave and mountain path lie hidden from the main road. Since the Third War, rogue Scourge have fortified the refuge under the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. They refused to serve the Dark Lady or flee north.

Ravenclaw's regents, guardians, and drudgers gathered in secret to prepare an assault on the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Forsaken scouts found them, and the quiet cliffs became a warzone. Now Horde fighters move against the undead before they can attack.

subzone:blackthorn-ridge.text: Blackthorn Ridge. At Blackthorn Ridge, Razormane quilboar guard the southern Barrens north of Razorfen Kraul. Brine, an orc shaman, keeps watch from a camp above a pool of unusually pure mountain water. Blackthorn Ridge rises beside Razorfen Kraul, its slopes crowded with dense thickets of sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar claim the ground as ancestral territory, using the thorny barriers to ambush outsiders and skirmish across the southern Barrens. Travelers seek out the ridge despite the danger, drawn to Brine, a hermit orc shaman. His camp sits above a spring famed across Kalimdor for its clear, spiritually pure water.

subzone:bladefist-bay.text: Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay opens onto the Great Sea along eastern Durotar, just beyond Orgrimmar's gates. Craggy bluffs rise above its shore, with Azshara's southern coast across the water. Bladefist Bay meets the Great Sea along Durotar's northeastern edge. Rocky cliffs rise above its treacherous surf, just east of Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. Across the water to the north, Azshara's ancient red cliffs and ruins mark the far shore. The bay forms a boundary between Durotar and the open sea. Kargath Bladefist gave the bay its name. Chieftain of the Shattered Hand clan, he severed his own hand and replaced it with a blade during the old Horde's trials on Draenor. Skull Rock lies nearby, where cultists and hidden rogue networks work in the shadows. The coast recalls the fierce, ruthless legacy of the clan's chieftain.

subzone:bloodhoof-village.text:
Bloodhoof Village. At Bloodhoof Village beside Stonebull Lake, young tauren prepare for the road to Thunder Bluff. Baine Bloodhoof leads them, while the village tends Mulgore’s defense, trade, and rites. Beside Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore, Bloodhoof Village is where young tauren come after their trials at Camp Narache. They hone their skills here before traveling to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. Patient breeders tame wild kodo beasts for travel, and the village is also a center of craft and ceremony. Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, oversees daily rule and the region’s defense. Braves patrol the grasslands against aggressive wildlife, quilboar encroachers, and the Venture Company.

Spiritual guides such as Zarlman Two-Moons tend to the tribe’s inner life. They lead novices through sacred journeys, including the Rite of Vision.

subzone:boulder-lode-mine.text: Boulder Lode Mine. In the northeastern Barrens, the Venture Company tears into Boulder Lode Mine for its riches. Orcish banners and watchtowers mark a claim the Horde once held. Weathered orcish works frame the mine mouth, signs that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Now Venture Company overseers and enforcers answer to Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strips the canyon for minerals, gems, and machinery, with little care for the land or its workers. Riches from the mine have drawn attention from Ratchet. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has sent mercenaries after a rumored massive emerald found in the tunnels. Engineers seeking to understand goblin machinery also know that Boss Copperplug keeps key operating manuals in his camp.

subzone:brambleblade-ravine.text: Brambleblade Ravine. Bristleback quilboar raid Camp Narache from Brambleblade Ravine, on Red Cloud Mesa’s northeastern edge. Young tauren braves enter the ravine to defend their homeland and prove their strength. Brambleblade Ravine cuts into Red Cloud Mesa’s northeastern edge, where thorny briars and quilboar camps shelter the Bristleback tribe. From there, the Bristlebacks raid Camp Narache and threaten young tauren coming of age. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the shamans and warriors who dwell deep in the ravine, alongside their trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the canyon is both a rite of passage and a hard need if the plains are to be safe.

subzone:bramblescar.text: Bramblescar. Across the southern Barrens, Bramblescar's Razormane wage war with the Bristleback across the Gold Road. Thick brambles fortify their settlement. Bramblescar is carved into the jagged briars of the southern Barrens. The thick, sharp thorns make a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar and deter casual wanderers. The tribe is fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders. They skirmish with anyone who approaches, treating all who are not quilboar as intruders on land blessed by their ancient boar gods. Bramblescar sits in perpetual tension with Agama'gor, the Bristleback encampment directly across the Gold Road. The rival tribes wage an unrelenting war for dominion over the southern Barrens. Razormane warriors fight Horde travelers along the highway and repel Bristleback raiding parties, keeping them on constant, violent alert.

subzone:brightwater-lake.text: Brightwater Lake. Across Tirisfal's lowlands, Brightwater Lake lies cold and dark northeast of Brill. Once a retreat for Lordaeron, it now surrounds an island where a lone necromancer conducts forbidden research. Brightwater Lake spreads across northern Tirisfal between Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post. Under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, its shores offered a quiet country haven. That peace is gone. The Plaguelands lie to the east, and grey skies hang over the lake's murky, chilled waters. Withered trees line the shore, where murlocs and hostile undead roam.

subzone:brill.text:
Brill. In Brill, Forsaken gather north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Newly awakened undead travel here from Deathknell, joining a rebuilt human town that now anchors Forsaken rule and arms in Tirisfal Glades. Before the Third War, Brill grew under nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. Then Kel'Thuzad chose the region for the Cult of the Damned's first experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The blight swept through the people so swiftly that the local militia fled. A vast graveyard remained for the dead.

Now Magistrate Sevren leads the Forsaken who have rebuilt Brill. Weathered Lordaeron buildings line its streets. The town coordinates defenses against Scarlet Crusade attacks, Scourge remnants, and native beasts changed by necromantic decay. Brill links Tirisfal Glades to the wider Horde. Goblins operate the zeppelin tower, carrying travelers south toward Durotar and deep into Stranglethorn Vale. Gallows' End Tavern offers shelter. Its cellar also holds captured Scarlet zealots for interrogation and apothecarial testing.

subzone:brill-town-hall.text: Brill Town Hall. In Brill Town Hall, the Forsaken govern Brill and plan Tirisfal's defense. Its doors stand in Lordaeron's shattered heart. Forsaken rule continues from Brill Town Hall while much of Lordaeron lies in ruins. Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium and gives orders to Forsaken travelers. Few known town halls remain active under Forsaken control. Beyond the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, Brill's hall is among them. It keeps Lordaeron's old civic order alive beneath undead rule.

subzone:burning-blade-coven.text: Burning Blade Coven. In the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven threatens the Horde’s newest recruits. Corrupted cultists and summoned demons haunt the old mineral caves, using them as a staging ground for dark magic on Durotar’s doorstep. Dark rituals now trouble the caves along the Valley of Trials’ northern edge. Imps and lesser fiends spill from the cavern mouth, stirring chaos and threatening the young orcs and Darkspear trolls who train here for service to the Horde. The Burning Blade cult has entrenched itself deep inside, led by the shadowy warlock Yarrog Baneshadow. What was a testing wilderness is now an active battleground against demonic corruption. Before demons took root in the caves, local overseers hoped to harvest their raw materials for the settlement. Foreman Thazz'ril ventured inside on a mineral survey, but the cultists drove him out in haste, and he left valuable equipment behind. Driving back Baneshadow's coven is now the ultimate proving trial for aspiring warriors, rogues, and spellcasters before they are deemed ready to venture into greater Durotar.

subzone:camp-taurajo.text: Camp Taurajo. Camp Taurajo holds the eastern mouth of the pass into Mulgore. The tauren camp offers travelers an inn, supplies, mentors, and wind rider routes across the plains and central Kalimdor. At Camp Taurajo, you reach the eastern mouth of the pass into Mulgore. For young tauren leaving Bloodhoof Village, the camp is often their first glimpse of the wider Barrens. Dry scrubland and rugged mesas surround this outpost and trading hub. Hunters, leathercrafters, and field herbalists find shelter here, while wind riders connect the camp to Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and Freewind Post deeper south.

subzone:canals-undercity.text: Canals (Undercity). In the Undercity, green slime fills the Canals between its quarters. The murky channels carry waste and mark the Forsaken's underground stronghold. Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, green sludge fills the Canals. The stone channels circle the Undercity and divide its quarters. They carry industrial refuse, chemical runoff, and alchemical waste instead of flowing water. Faint light shines through the liquid, and foul vapors rise from it. Water Walking cannot carry anyone across. Still, desperate anglers sometimes pull strange, tainted curiosities from the muck.

subzone:cavern-of-mists.text: Cavern of Mists. The Cavern of Mists is the expansive outer antechamber leading into the depths of the Wailing Caverns. Fed by subterranean geysers that erupt through the rock, its central pool and hanging fog harbor strange, mutated wildlife roaming just outside the portal threshold. Before descending into the true heart of the Wailing Caverns, travelers must navigate the Cavern of Mists. Thick, warm vapor hangs permanently in the air, fed by natural geysers erupting from the cavern floor into a deep central pool. Though it serves as an entryway, it is far from peaceful. Swarms of raptors, serpents, oozes, and semi-aquatic threshadons wander the ledges and waters, alongside notorious beasts like the hydra Trigore the Lasher. It provides adventurers an ominous preview of the unnatural growth festering deeper below.

subzone:cleft-of-shadow.text: Cleft of Shadow. Rogues, warlocks, and their teachers gather in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. The caverns give them room to practice their arts under the Horde's watch. Below Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow holds rogues of the Shadowswift Brotherhood and warlocks of the Darkfire Enclave. Thrall's Horde honors shamanism and strength of arms, yet its leaders make room for subtler arts. In these caverns, practitioners of poison and fel energy work away from the valley districts and under Orgrimmar's watch. At the Cleft's lowest point, a passage opens into Ragefire Chasm. Volcanic caves honeycomb the ground beneath Orgrimmar, and their danger draws defenders and sinister cultists to the cavern's edge.

subzone:cold-hearth-manor.text:
Cold Hearth Manor. Along Tirisfal’s main road, Forsaken guards hold Cold Hearth Manor west of Brill. Once a farm that fed Lordaeron, it fell to the Plague of Undeath, and Scourge now haunt its fields. Forsaken guards hold the farmhouse at Cold Hearth Manor, west of Brill along Tirisfal’s main road. Before the Third War, the estate was known for warm hospitality and rich harvests in the heart of Lordaeron.

When the Plague swept through the kingdom, the family and their laborers died and rose again as husks bound to the Scourge. Feral undead still wander the ruined fields, but Forsaken forces drove the mindless dead from the farmhouse. They now use it as a trading post and foothold on the road toward the eastern glades.

subzone:crag-of-the-everliving.text: Crag of the Everliving. The Crag of the Everliving is a verdant cavern chamber nestled deep within the Wailing Caverns. Dominated by lush, corrupted flora and predatory plant creatures, it serves as the domain of the Fanglord Lord Pythas. Its towering upper reaches shelter the ancient entity after whom the crag is named. While much of the Wailing Caverns is carved of damp subterranean stone, the Crag of the Everliving bursts with unruly, twisted vegetation fueled by the Nightmare corrupting Naralex's slumber. Towering mossy platforms and winding paths are choked with Deviate Shamblers—living plant hulks prowling the undergrowth. Lord Pythas, one of Naralex's fallen disciples, watches over the crag's central reaches, having traded his noble druidic vows for the venomous rites of the Druids of the Fang. The chamber draws its name from Verdan the Everliving, a colossal, primordial plant elemental who resides in the crag's upper heights. Corrupted by the Emerald Nightmare that grips the cavern, Verdan now acts as a fearsome line of defense rather than a peaceful natural guardian. Beyond his towering form lurks Lord Serpentis, the self-proclaimed chief of the Fanglords, who oversees the sect's descent into serpentine madness.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company.
